title: Microturn Orchestra and Typed Ledgers — PRD Brainstorm
body:
Purpose
This doc collects a focused set of ideas for a lightweight PRD: a streaming-first API surface that enables low-latency "microturns", predictable tool invocation semantics, and a compact, typed ledger for structured outputs and resumable client SDKs. This is a brainstorm / working draft aimed at giving engineering and SDK teams concrete tradeoffs to evaluate before we pick a single surface to prototype.

Context and motivation
- Problem: Many host integrations need fast interactive loops (e.g., chat with quick clarifying microturns, step-by-step code edits, in-editor assistants). Current hosted streaming surfaces either emit long monolithic deltas (high latency to actionable partials) or require heavy client-side parsing and heuristics that leak complexity to customers. Tool calls complicate streaming further: clients need deterministic boundaries, idempotency, and a recoverable history.
- Goal: Provide an API shape that (a) surfaces actionable partial responses quickly (microturns), (b) gives deterministic tool-call boundaries and typed metadata, and (c) makes client resume/replay trivial with a compact typed ledger and resume tokens. Keep SDK surface minimal for first pass.

Key user stories
1) Editor assistant: user types a short clarification question; assistant emits intent -> if tool needed, emits a tool-call frame quickly, otherwise emits short actionable text. Client wants to show partial output within 50–120ms for microturns.
2) Multi-step workflow: assistant alternates between generating text and invoking a code-run tool. If client disconnects, they can resume from the last typed ledger entry and continue without re-executing side-effects.
3) Mobile low-bandwidth: client can request compact updates (summary-only) and selectively fetch full frames later.

Design primitives (high level)
- Microturn: an atomic partial response unit optimized for short, interruptible interactions. Typical microturns are < 300 tokens; aim for 1–5 partial frames per user turn in many flows. Microturns are delivered as streaming frames with explicit boundaries.
- Typed Ledger: append-only, ordered ledger of typed frames emitted during a session. Each ledger entry is small (type, minimal metadata, optional compact payload hash), and the client can request full payloads by id. Ledger entries are authoritative and can be checkpointed in the control plane for resume.
- Tool-call Frame: a first-class frame type in the ledger. Tool-call frames include: tool_id, args_schema_ref, call_id (idempotency key), expected_side_effects (bitmask), and a pre-checksum of args for validation. Tool-call frames also support a status lifecycle (requested, dispatched, completed, failed, fallback).
- Resume Token / Checkpoint: serialized pointer into the ledger (sequence number + checksum + optional short proof). Resume token allows restarting without re-playing completed side-effects; server guarantees that ledger entries marked completed have committed side-effects or an at-most-once guarantee depending on setting.

API surface sketch (informal)
- POST /v1/sessions (body: model, mode: microturn, resume_token?) -> session_id + resume_token
- PATCH /v1/sessions/:id/append (streaming/multipart) -> stream of ledger-frame events (types below). Response: checkpoint updates and an optional compact ledger delta.
- GET /v1/sessions/:id/ledger?from=seq -> list of typed ledger entries (compact)
- POST /v1/sessions/:id/tool-results/:call_id -> tool provider posts results (webhook or pull)

Ledger frame types (examples)
- text.partial: user-visible partial text chunk (microturn)
- text.commit: final text for a microturn
- tool.call: request to invoke tool (args optional compressed blob)
- tool.result: typed structured result (json schema id + compact body)
- checkpoint: server-generated durable checkpoint (sequence + resume token)
- error: recoverable or terminal error with code and remediation hints

SDK ergonomics (principles)
- Single-stream model: SDK exposes session lifecycle + a simple event callback for ledger frames. No heavy parsing for clients; library converts typed frames into typed objects.
- Compact subscription: clients can register to receive full frames or only ledger summaries. Summary mode receives only frame headers (type, seq, small human snippet) and fetches full body on demand.
- Resume API: SDK exposes resume(session_id, resume_token) that internally fetches ledger delta and reconciles outstanding tool calls; SDK surfaces a single recover() callback for apps to reconcile UI state and rehydrate in-memory tool caches.
- Minimal surface: avoid exposing raw protocol tokens/frames to application code; prefer typed objects + high-level helpers (e.g., requestToolCall(toolId, args) -> Promise(toolResult)).

Degree of guarantees and modes
- Modes: best-effort (low-latency microturns, tool calls may be retried), transactional-safe (slower, server ensures at-most-once semantics for tool side-effects using durable commit), audit-mode (ledger fully persisted + audit id). Customers choose mode at session creation.
- Latency vs safety tradeoff: best-effort prioritizes returning microturn frames to client quickly (assistive UI). Transactional-safe will introduce commit fences (extra RTT) for tool.call events.

Observability and debugging
- Telemetry: emit per-frame latency, token counts, tool-call lifecycle durations, resume/replay counts, SDK-sideframe fetch counts.
- SDK exposes a debugDump() that returns a short textual ledger snapshot for support flows.

Rollout plan (proposal)
- Week 0–2: implement server-side ledger prototype (in-memory) + simple streaming frame emitter. Basic typed frames for text.partial, text.commit, tool.call, tool.result.
- Week 3–5: build a minimal JS SDK (browser + node) that implements subscription modes (summary & full) + resume helper. Hook to an internal tool-mock service.
- Week 6–8: integrate durability mode: durable checkpointing to store and resume without double-execution; add server-side idempotency checks.
- Week 9–12: run 3 internal playtests (editor-assistant, code-run, mobile-slim) and measure: median microturn latency, resume success rate, tool-call double-execution rate.

Metrics (success criteria)
- Median first microturn latency <= 120ms for simple prompts under P50 load.
- Resume success rate >= 99% for disconnected sessions (no lost side-effects in transactional-safe mode).
- Tool-call double-execution <= 0.1% in transactional-safe mode.
- SDK adoption: 10 internal teams experimenting within 8 weeks.

Open questions (prioritized)
1) Ledger size limits: what retention/snapshot policy avoids unbounded growth while enabling useful resume windows? (e.g., keep last 1k entries or 24h)
2) Side-effect semantics: how do we mark tool calls that are non-idempotent? Do we require tool providers to implement compensating actions or rely on transactional-safe mode?
3) Security: what metadata can we safely include in compact ledger entries without leaking PII to third-party SDKs or logs?
4) Mobile bandwidth: should the SDK perform automatic delta compression for microturns, or leave this to app code?
5) Billing model: ledger entries + resume storage add storage/compute costs; charge per-session-storage? per-checkpoint?

Non-goals
- Not aiming to be a universal RPC platform for arbitrary tool graphs. This PRD focuses on single-session, sequential microturn flows and direct tool invocations. Complex distributed tool orchestration is out-of-scope for initial prototype.

Implementation risks and mitigations
- Risk: Tool double-execution in best-effort mode will confuse customers. Mitigation: clearly document semantics, provide default transactional-safe for any tool flagged non-idempotent, and add server-side idempotency helpers.
- Risk: SDK complexity ballooning if we support too many subscription modes. Mitigation: ship only two modes (summary & full) and a tiny helper for resumable merges.
- Risk: Ledger retention costs. Mitigation: configurable retention per org + cheap compressed headers for older entries.

Next steps (immediate)
- Product & Eng alignment meeting: pick tradeoff defaults (default to best-effort microturns, transactional-safe optional) — target Nov 18 sync.
- Engineering spike: implement in-memory ledger prototype + JS SDK stub — owner: Jonah Li — 2w spike.
- Ask Security: quick review on ledger header PII leakage — owner: Priya — due Nov 10.

Notes / rough sketches
- Example microturn stream sequence (headers only):
  1: text.partial {seq:1, hint: "Summarizing…"}
  2: tool.call {seq:2, tool_id:run-unit-test, call_id:c7, args_hash:abcd}
  3: tool.result {seq:3, tool_id:run-unit-test, call_id:c7, status:completed, schema:run-result-v1}
  4: text.commit {seq:4, text: "All tests passing"}
- Resume token: "s-123:seq4:sha256(ledger-4):m=best" (opaque to client but SDK can show human readable checkpoint time).

Appendix: low-fidelity API examples and pseudo-frames
- text.partial frame (summary mode): {type:"text.partial", seq:17, ttl_preview:120, snippet:"Looks like a missing import"}
- tool.call (compact header): {type:"tool.call", seq:18, tool_id:"lint-check", call_id:"c-18", args_ref:"arg-18", expected_side_effects:0}
- tool.result (full fetch URL optional): {type:"tool.result", seq:19, schema:"lint-v1", body_ref:"ref://payload/19"}

-- end --

(Feel free to rearrange. This is intentionally a loose PRD brainstorm; the goal is to converge on a single API surface to prototype.)
